title: Tenant fence chronicle compiler: automated residency & retention reporting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers running Redwood Dedicated require concise, auditable artifacts proving tenant isolation and residency over time plus evidence that retention policies were applied. Current evidence exports are scattered (telemetry blobs, node manifests, ad-hoc snapshots) and are expensive to assemble during audits.

Goal: Build a pipeline (the "Chronicle Compiler") that compiles per-tenant tenancy events, region bindings, retention lifecycle actions, and notarized node manifests into human- and machine-readable attestations. Output should be: (1) a compact daily summary (ndjson) for audit ingestion, (2) a notarized tarball for legal/compliance packaging, and (3) a streaming audit feed for SOC and SRE.

Scope: Dedicated capacity only. Inputs: tenant-to-node bindings, region map, retention policy events (delete/expire/hold), storage lifecycle logs, and runbook actions. Outputs: chronicle-summary.ndjson, chronicle-package-<tenant>-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz (with signatures), and a streaming topic to the compliance topic.

Constraints and non-goals: This ticket does not change eviction/placement logic. It focuses on evidence assembly and retention reporting. Preservation of PII in exported artifacts is controlled by tenant-level export flags and redaction rules documented in the design doc.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket and attached PRD. Early design reviewed with PM and Compliance. Agreed outputs: ndjson summary, signed tarball, and kafka stream. Asked infra to estimate storage impact.

2026-03-03 — Miguel Torres: Spike complete. Implemented local prototype that consumes tenant-binding events and emits ndjson lines. Prototype stored one day of data in /tmp and produced a tar.gz containing a manifest.json and minimal telemetry. Observed ~2.3KB per-tenant/day for standard footprint in eu-west nodes.

2026-03-05 — Compliance (Dana Liu): Request — signed artifacts must include a chainable signature header (timestamp + signer id) compatible with legal format. Recommended using existing key-management integration (KMS) for signing and storing public keys in a Verified Keys registry.

2026-03-07 — Miguel Torres: Design update — will produce two signature types: KMS-signed envelope for customers who use Redwood KMS, and an unsigned-but-hash-signed artifact for Private deployments where customer manages KMS. Added key rotation metadata to manifest.

2026-03-08 — PM (Rajiv Menon): Prioritized retention enforcement mapping. Chronicle should record the rationale for retention decisions (policy id + evaluation timestamp) and include a link to the deletion job that executed the action.
2026-03-09 — Security (Priya Raman): Flagged that export must support automated redaction rules for PII. Suggested a redaction pipeline stage that runs before packaging. Added as action item.

2026-03-10 — Miguel Torres: Implemented streaming exporter to compliance.kafka/topic-chronicles. Added schema v1 (fields: tenant_id, date, region, node_ids, retention_policy_id, retention_action, manifest_hash, signatures). Draft PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345

2026-03-11 — Design (Lina Gomez): Reviewed exported summary sample. UX concern: auditors need human-readable timeline in addition to ndjson. Agreed to attach a rendered HTML timeline as optional attachment in the tarball.

2026-03-12 — Miguel Torres: Integration test notes — hooking into region-mapper service uncovered missing region tag on nodes in eu-central; filed ENG-840200 to patch node tag propagation. Workaround: compiler will enrich node metadata from instance registry for now.

2026-03-13 — Aisha Patel: Ready for internal security review. Miguel to open final PR and attach runbook for operational recovery and retention corrections. Next: add e2e test that runs a simulated tenant through retention lifecycle and validates artifact integrity and signatures.
acceptance_criteria: Daily ndjson summary produced for every Dedicated tenant that opts in to evidence exports
Signed tarball containing manifest.json, per-tenant timeline (HTML optional), and node manifests is produced and stored for configured retention window
Streaming feed publishes chronicle events to compliance.kafka/topic-chronicles with schema v1
Artifacts include key metadata (signer id, key version, manifest_hash) and pass signature verification using the Verified Keys registry
Export pipeline enforces tenant redaction flags and documents any skipped fields in manifest.json
Operational runbook for on-demand historical compile and revocation procedure is published
